trial_court: Family Court, Imphal East, Mat (Divorce) Case No. 49 of 2018
case_name: Shri Prasant Sahu vs Smt. Priyanka Kumari
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent were married in 2016. Respondent gave birth to a child in 2016. Petitioner filed for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Ex parte decree was passed but set aside later.

legal_principles.principle: The power to order medical tests should be exercised only when it is expedient in the interest of justice.
legal_principles.held: Relying on the decisions of the Supreme Court, the Family Court opined that the power to order medical tests should be exercised only when it is expedient in the interest of justice.
cited_cases: Banarsi Dass Vs. Teeku Dutta (Mrs.) & anr., (2005) 4 SCC 449
Kamti Devi Vs. Poshi Ram, (2001) 5 SCC 311

legal_principles.principle: A DNA test cannot rebut the presumption envisaged under Section 112 of the Evidence Act, 1872.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court accordingly denied the request for DNA testing to ascertain whether the petitioner-husband was the biological father of the child.
cited_cases: Banarsi Dass Vs. Teeku Dutta (Mrs.) & anr., (2005) 4 SCC 449
Kamti Devi Vs. Poshi Ram, (2001) 5 SCC 311

outcome.final_order: Petitioner's appeal allowed; case restored to file.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
